settings.headline: Started on a vacant lot
settings.subtitle: Commonground is a member-led nonprofit. Members elect the board, set our policy priorities and decide how surplus dues are spent.

settings.headline: From one garden to
settings.body:
Commonground began when twelve gardeners in Philadelphia fought to keep a lot they had farmed for six years. They won, and then got calls from gardeners in other cities who wanted to know how.

Today we are a national association of 3,400 members in eight chapters. We publish toolkits, train new garden leaders, run a group insurance policy and track land-use rules in 40 cities.

We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded mostly by member dues. Our books are open: the annual report and audited accounts are in the member library.
settings.quote: A garden on a vacant lot is the cheapest public park a city will ever get.

settings.headline: Four things,
settings.subtitle: Everything we do comes back to keeping community gardens growing.

items.title: Train garden leaders
items.text: A six-week course for new coordinators, run twice a year in every chapter.

items.title: Protect land
items.text: Policy tracking, legal clinics and member action when a garden is at risk.

items.title: Share what works
items.text: A library of toolkits and templates, free to members, written by members.

items.title: Fund new gardens
items.text: Half of Supporter dues go to new gardens in neighbourhoods without fresh food.

settings.headline: There is a plot
settings.subtitle: Join a chapter, come to an event or talk to us about starting one where you live.
